audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does the request-response client enforce count * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS response limit?

phase1_summary.relevant_excerpt: The P2P network code uses max_request_data_column_sidecars (0x4000) as the limit. The response is limited via .take(max_request_data_column_sidecars). However, the spec also requires count * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS limit which may be stricter for small count values.
phase1_summary.initial_assessment: The code enforces MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS but needs verification that count * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS is also enforced for small count values.

gaps_identified: The count-based limit (count * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS) may not be explicitly enforced separately from MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS
phase2_summary.attack_surface: A peer could potentially return more sidecars than count * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS for small count values, up to MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS

phase3_summary.exploitability: Requires malicious peer to send oversized response
phase3_summary.recommendation: Verify that both limits are enforced: min(count * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS, MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS)

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does the beacon-node server limit DataColumnSidecarsByRange responses to count * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS?

phase1_summary.relevant_excerpt: Server-side response construction uses .take(max_request_data_column_sidecars) to limit responses. The count * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS limit needs separate verification.
phase1_summary.initial_assessment: Server enforces MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS but count-based limit needs verification.

gaps_identified: Need to verify count * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS is applied as an additional constraint
phase2_summary.attack_surface: Server may send more sidecars than expected for small count values

phase3_summary.exploitability: Low - would require specific count values
phase3_summary.recommendation: Audit the request parsing to ensure count-based limits are applied

audit_items.title: Falsification Test: Can a response exceed count * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS sidecars for a small count value?

phase1_summary.relevant_excerpt: The response handling code applies .take(max_request_data_column_sidecars) limit. For count=1 with NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS=128, the spec limit is 128, but MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS is 0x4000 (16384).
phase1_summary.initial_assessment: Falsification test requires checking if count * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS is enforced separately.

gaps_identified: Cannot definitively confirm count-based limit without integration testing
phase2_summary.attack_surface: If only MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS is enforced, small count requests could return up to 16384 sidecars instead of count * 128

phase3_summary.exploitability: Requires crafted request with small count value
phase3_summary.recommendation: Create integration test with count=1 and verify response <= 128 sidecars

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Is the data column sidecar inclusion proof correctly verified via verify_data_column_sidecar_inclusion_proof?

phase1_summary.relevant_excerpt: verify_sidecar_inclusion_proof(&data_column_sidecar, metrics) is called with ensure! macro, resulting in REJECT if proof is invalid.
phase1_summary.initial_assessment: Inclusion proof verification is correctly enforced in the gossip validation pipeline.

phase2_summary.attack_surface: None identified - inclusion proof verification is mandatory

phase3_summary.recommendation: Property holds. The code correctly verifies inclusion proofs.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does actor-p2p-peer relay only data column sidecars with valid inclusion proofs?

phase1_summary.relevant_excerpt: The validation ensures inclusion proof is verified before any relay action. Invalid sidecars result in Error::DataColumnSidecarInvalidInclusionProof.
phase1_summary.initial_assessment: P2P peers validate inclusion proofs before relay.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does actor-beacon-node reject sidecars with invalid inclusion proofs from any source?

phase1_summary.relevant_excerpt: The validation code checks inclusion proof for non-EL origins. For EL origins (locally produced blocks), the proof is implicitly trusted as generated by the node itself.
phase1_summary.initial_assessment: Inclusion proofs are verified for P2P-received sidecars. EL-origin sidecars skip this check as they are locally generated.

phase2_summary.attack_surface: EL-origin path bypass is intentional for locally-produced data

audit_items.title: Falsification Test: Can a sidecar with an invalid inclusion proof be accepted by the gossip validation pipeline?

phase1_summary.relevant_excerpt: verify_sidecar_inclusion_proof uses is_valid_merkle_branch to cryptographically verify the proof against the block body root. The function returns false for invalid proofs.
phase1_summary.initial_assessment: Falsification would require bypassing cryptographic Merkle proof verification, which is not feasible.

phase3_summary.recommendation: Property holds. Invalid inclusion proofs are rejected.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Is verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs called for every data column sidecar in the gossip validation pipeline?

phase1_summary.relevant_excerpt: verify_kzg_proofs(&data_column_sidecar, self.store_config.kzg_backend, metrics) is called unconditionally for non-EL origins, with error handling that rejects invalid sidecars.
phase1_summary.initial_assessment: KZG proof verification is enforced for all externally-received sidecars.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does actor-p2p-peer enforce KZG proof verification before relaying data column sidecars?

phase1_summary.relevant_excerpt: KZG proof verification occurs before the sidecar action is returned. Failed verification results in Error::DataColumnSidecarInvalidKzgProofs which causes rejection.
phase1_summary.initial_assessment: KZG proofs are verified before relay.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does actor-beacon-node reject sidecars with invalid KZG proofs from any source?

phase1_summary.relevant_excerpt: For non-EL origins, verify_kzg_proofs is called and failures are propagated as errors. EL-origin sidecars bypass this as they are locally constructed.
phase1_summary.initial_assessment: External sidecars require valid KZG proofs.

phase2_summary.attack_surface: EL bypass is intentional for local data

audit_items.title: Falsification Test: Can a sidecar with tampered column data and invalid KZG proofs be accepted by the gossip validation pipeline?

phase1_summary.relevant_excerpt: verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch delegates to backend-specific verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_raw implementations (BLST, Arkworks, etc.) which perform cryptographic verification.
phase1_summary.initial_assessment: KZG proof verification is cryptographically sound - tampered data will fail verification.

audit_items.title: Verify Pre-Condition Ordering: Does KZG proof verification occur after structural and signature validation?

phase1_summary.relevant_excerpt: Validation order: 1) verify_data_column_sidecar (structural), 2) signature verification for proposer, 3) verify_sidecar_inclusion_proof, 4) verify_kzg_proofs. KZG is last.
phase1_summary.initial_assessment: KZG verification occurs after structural and signature checks, as per spec.

phase2_summary.attack_surface: Correct ordering prevents DoS via expensive KZG ops on invalid inputs
